After about two years of construction, the Institute for Hearing Technology and Acoustics (IHTA) at RWTH Aachen University has moved into the newly completed Cube 3 building at Kopernikusstraße 18 in Aachen, Germany. One floor holds the institute’s offices and meeting rooms. Another brings the mechanical and electronics workshops together with all of the laboratories, which, the institute says with gratitude and some pride, now places it among the best-equipped acoustics institutes.

The new facilities include a hemi-anechoic chamber of about 95 m² and 520 m³ that meets the accuracy grade 1 (precision) requirements of DIN EN ISO 3745, with a lower cutoff frequency of 100 Hz and measurements up to 20 kHz; a fully anechoic chamber of about 50 m² and 316 m³, also grade 1, covering 125 Hz–20 kHz; a reverberation room of about 300 m³ with highly reflective surfaces for measurements to ISO 354; an acoustic virtual reality lab designed to the listening-room requirements of ITU-R BS.1116; three audiometric booths built as room-within-a-room structures with integrated absorbers, compliant with common hearing-test standards; and the two workshops.

The team is still unpacking and fitting out the labs. Most of the experimental setups should be running by early 2027, among them SCaLAr, a 68-channel loudspeaker array, and a 64-channel system for fast measurement of individual head-related transfer functions (HRTFs). The architects, RKW Architektur +, describe the building on their project page.

Adapted into Chinese by Fanyu Meng from a LinkedIn post by Janina Fels, head of IHTA; all photos come from that post. Read the original.
